doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: A working musician's week, finances, marriage and green card status
summary: No typical week; he plays a Tuesday jam session, does not teach, accepts financial worry, and mentions a 17-year marriage ended in divorce.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: That’s a really interesting outlook. What’s a typical week like for you?
I mean like, being a working musician, what do you do during a particular week? Do you do a lot of different things?
Yeah. A lot of different things. I cannot say this week or that week or this month or that month. Every year, every time it’s different. I cannot predict anything.
So what do you do besides play with Junior?
I play with other people. Every Tuesday I have a jam session, a house band. I don’t teach. I just play.
You’re just a player. Is it — I don’t know how to ask this — is it an easy life?

For me. For me it’s easy. Because I don’t have any choice. I really wanted to live this way. And I went to school in Japan too, but I really wanted to play, just play. I’m not a good teacher so — because if you know this way, then it’s so many things, financial you know. Yes of course I am sometimes scared of financial things, but now I am 58 years. There’s always something bad happening. Then next time something’s happening. Like okay. After nine years I’m an illegal alien, and nine years I’m just playing in the street, and you know, I started thinking of going back to Japan because I didn’t have any career, just playing on the street. Then I got the green card. So that means, you must stay. Okay, okay. And after I got the green card I married. I divorced already. But I had a good 17 years. It’s always something.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. I think so.
And are you a citizen now?
No. But I have a green card.
Okay. So you can stay here.
